name: index_momentum_stock_selection_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY has established >0.5% return from the day's open by 10:00 IST, large institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms executing buy-side mandates (FII inflows, mutual fund SIPs deployed intraday) remain active through the morning session, absorbing short-term supply and creating a persistent directional bias. At 5-second resolution, this regime manifests as a drift where 2-minute counter-moves are quickly followed by resumptions — the institutional buy queue has not cleared. A bearish morning regime (NIFTY down >0.5% from open) creates the mirror dynamic with seller-driven TWAP flow overwhelming intraday bounces. We confirm the regime is still live with a 2-minute spot return aligned to the morning direction before entering, filtering dips/pops that temporarily break the regime.

indicators.name: morning_return
indicators.purpose: Cumulative return from the day's opening price — the regime filter. This is a fixed-time cumulative measure (same concept as the original's 10:00 snapshot), not scaled from the original lookback. Establishes whether institutional flow is net bullish or bearish for the morning session. No lookback scaling needed because it's a running sum since day open, not a rolling window.

indicators.name: fast_ret_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute return (24 x 5s bars) as the intraday entry trigger confirming the regime is still active. The original made a single daily entry at 10:00 and held 1.5-4 hours. We hold 15-120 seconds, so the entry trigger must be compressed to match our hold time. A 2-minute lookback (24 bars) is the natural fast-momentum confirmation — long enough to filter 5-second noise, short enough to reflect current micro-momentum. 12x scaling from original would give 12 bars (1 min), but 24 bars (2 min) is chosen because the regime needs a slightly longer confirmation to avoid whipsaws in moderate-trend days.

conditions: morning_return > 0.5% (NIFTY is in bullish morning regime — institutional buying active)
fast_ret_24 > 0.05% (2-minute return positive — regime is live, not reversing)
vix < 22 (avoid high-vol regime where morning momentum reverses quickly)
buy_ce.confirmation: Both the daily regime signal and the 2-minute fast return must agree on the bullish direction

conditions: morning_return < -0.5% (NIFTY is in bearish morning regime — institutional selling active)
fast_ret_24 < -0.05% (2-minute return negative — regime is live, not reversing)
buy_pe.confirmation: Both the daily regime signal and the 2-minute fast return must agree on the bearish direction

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points (~8 NIFTY spot points at ATM delta ~0.5): if NIFTY retraces 8+ spot points against the morning regime direction within 120 seconds, the institutional TWAP flow has temporarily paused or the regime has shifted, invalidating the micro-thesis. A 4-point stop limits loss to ~6.7x breakeven and avoids holding through regime breaks.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points (~14 NIFTY spot points): within a bullish/bearish morning regime, 2-minute momentum continuations on NIFTY typically cover 10-20 spot points; 14 pts captures 50-70% of the median continuation move, producing a 1:1.75 R:R. This is consistent with the 1-2 minute typical move of 3-7 option pts (we target the upper-mid range where regime strength adds conviction).

filters.vix_filter: vix < 22 — same as original strategy; high-vol sessions see morning momentum reverse sharply, destroying regime persistence
filters.time_filter: 10:00-14:30 IST; regime established after 45 minutes of trading, and afternoon sessions after 14:30 see regime exhaustion and mean-reversion
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume is always sufficient for limit order execution
filters.trend_filter: morning_return > |0.5%| from day open is the primary regime filter
filters.spread_filter: limit order execution at candle close — no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — morning momentum persistence is a known effect, but the regime filter (>0.5%) provides selectivity. Primary risk is afternoon mean-reversion after strong morning moves degrading later-session trades.

adaptation_notes: The original strategy used beta-sorted stock selection (top 5 highest-beta Nifty50 stocks) to amplify index momentum. The stock selection mechanism is entirely dropped — trading NIFTY ATM options directly provides inherent index beta exposure. The core alpha signal (NIFTY morning momentum regime established by 10:00) is preserved as the primary regime filter. Hold time is compressed from 90-240 minutes to 15-120 seconds, requiring a fast 2-minute entry trigger rather than a single daily entry at 10:00. VIX filter preserved at threshold 22. Session window matches original (10:00-14:30). The beta amplification concept is replaced by ATM option delta (~0.5), which naturally amplifies index moves.
weaknesses: Regime can reverse intraday — afternoon mean-reversion after strong morning moves will generate losing trades in later session
On days where morning return is near threshold (0.4-0.6%), signal quality degrades — regime is ambiguous
Multiple trades in same direction within regime creates correlated losses if regime reverses sharply
VIX < 22 filter may miss profitable trending days during moderate elevated-vol environments (VIX 22-25)
No stock-level beta amplification — pure NIFTY direction, not the 1.5x leverage the original achieved via stock selection
